To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a high-throughput screening method for identifying MOFs with high selectivity for CO2 adsorption in the presence of H2O was developed, (ii) the method uses an approximate method for calculating framework charges to screen a large number of MOFs and then uses accurate charges to perform detailed simulations of a small number of MOFs, and (iii) the screening method is general and can be used to identify MOFs for other gas separations.
MOFs with open metal sites and polar functional groups have the best performance in terms of CO2/H2O selectivity, and that the electrostatic interactions contribute most of the adsorption of H2O.

the electrostatic interactions are the dominant factor in determining the adsorption energy for H2O in MOFs, and that the use of fast, approximate charge calculation methods in screening studies can lead to the discovery of MOFs with high selectivity for CO2 over H 2O.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of novel materials for CO2 capture.
the development of new adsorbents for CO2 capture.
the computational screening of MOFs for CO2 capture, and we have demonstrated the importance of electrostatic interactions in adsorption of CO2 and H2O in MOFs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of accurate partial charges is crucial for the accurate simulation of water adsorption in porous materials.
MOFs with high selectivity for CO2 over H 2 O can be found using computational screening.
the use of accurate framework charges is essential for predicting CO2 adsorption in the presence of H2O.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MOF-5 and UiO-66 are the most promising MOFs for selective CO2 capture over H2O, and that the charge calculation method used for initial screening is sufficient to identify MOFs for detailed investigation.
MOFs with open metal sites are more suitable than those with closed metal sites for the adsorption of CO2 and water molecules.
MOF-177 is a promising adsorbent material for CO2 capture in the presence of H2O, and it can be used as a reference material for further studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the electrostatic interactions between water molecules and the framework are more important than the interactions between water and the adsorbate (CO2) for the adsorption of water in the selected MOF systems.
it is possible to design MOF materials that have high selectivity toward adsorbing CO2 over water.
the use of fast charge calculation methods can be used to identify promising MOFs for CO2 capture, and that further investigation of the most promising MOFs is warranted.
